rationales: Seven valence electrons is typical of halogens, not noble gases.
Most noble gases have eight valence electrons, although helium has two.
Nine is not the usual number of valence electrons in noble gases.
Ten is not the usual number of valence electrons in noble gases.
The modern periodic table has seven periods.
The modern periodic table has eight groups in some older classifications, not eight periods.
Ten is not the number of periods in the modern periodic table.
Eighteen is the number of groups, not periods, in the modern periodic table.
The K shell can hold a maximum of two electrons.
Eight is the maximum for the L shell, not the K shell.
Eighteen is the maximum for the M shell, not the K shell.
Thirty-two is the maximum for the N shell, not the K shell.
Fog is liquid water droplets dispersed in air, not a solid-in-solid solution.
Brass is an alloy in which solid zinc is dissolved in solid copper.
Cheese is not the standard example of a solid solute in a solid solvent.
Air is a mixture of gases, not a solid-in-solid solution.
800 °C is close to sodium chloride's melting point, not its boiling point.
850 °C is not the boiling point of sodium chloride.
1412 °C is close but is not the stated textbook value.
Sodium chloride's boiling point is given as 1413 °C.

3.8 is below fluorine's accepted Pauling electronegativity.
Fluorine's electronegativity is approximately 4.0 on the Pauling scale.
3.5 is below fluorine's accepted Pauling electronegativity.

KCl dissolves readily in water.
Benzene is insoluble in water.
Petrol is insoluble in water.
A p subshell has three orbitals, so it can hold more than four electrons.
Three p orbitals hold a maximum of six electrons.
Eight is not the maximum capacity of a p subshell.
Ten is the maximum capacity of a d subshell, not a p subshell.
Mass number is not the basis for arranging elements in the modern periodic table.
Avogadro’s number is unrelated to the table’s arrangement.
The modern periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number.
Quantum number is not the basis for arranging the periodic table.
Iron is much less dense than osmium.
Platinum is very dense but is less dense than osmium.
Osmium is the densest naturally occurring metal and is commonly called the heaviest metal.
Lead is heavy but is less dense than osmium.
Methane contains four single covalent C–H bonds.
Methane has no double bond.
Methane has no triple bond.
Methane does not contain a dative covalent bond.
Iodine is less electronegative than fluorine.
Bromine is less electronegative than fluorine.

Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among the halogens.

A metallic bond forms among metal atoms, not between two non-metals.
Two non-metals generally form a covalent bond by sharing electrons.
An ionic bond usually forms between a metal and a non-metal by electron transfer.
A coordinate covalent bond requires the shared pair to be donated by one atom and is not the general expected bond here.
The third period contains more than two elements.
The third period contains eight elements, from sodium to argon.
Eighteen elements occur in the fourth and fifth periods, not the third.
Thirty-two elements occur in the sixth and seventh periods, not the third.
